sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1903. Languages of the Kamilaroi and other Aboriginal tribes of New South Wales. Journal of the Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland 33: 259-283 ('The Darkinung language' pp. 271-275; 'Vocabulary of Darkinung words' pp. 280-282). Open copy: Zenodo/BHL record 1449596; archive.org scanned of JRAI vol. 33.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Orthography' section (pp. 260-261) describes letters and sounds only; the Darkinung grammar abstract (nouns, pronouns, verbs) and the ~330-word Darkinung vocabulary carry no statement on accent and no accent marks; 'accent'/'stress'/'emphasis' do not occur anywhere in the article (checked in both the JSTOR text layer and the archive.org scanned).

sources.citation: Jones, Caroline 2008. Darkinyung grammar and dictionary: revitalising a language from historical sources. Nambucca Heads, NSW: Muurrbay Aboriginal Language and Culture Co-operative. x+182 pp. ISBN 978-0-9775351-9-4.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL7001 .J66 2008
sources.note: The only modern linguistic description of Darkinyung (Glottolog's top-ranked reference; the earlier scan also named it). Muurrbay salvage grammars of neighbouring languages (Lissarrague 2006 HRLM, 2007 Dhanggati) include a stress paragraph, so this is where a stress statement, or an explicit 'not recoverable from the sources', would be.
